title: Acting President Iliana Yotova Wins Bulgaria's Presidential Runoff
dek: With all votes counted Monday, the Central Election Commission gave Yotova 57.6% to Andrey Gyurov's 39.5%, making her Bulgaria's first elected female head of state.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Parliament Square in Sofia, Bulgaria (file photo)

keyPoints: With all votes counted on Monday, Bulgaria's Central Election Commission gave Acting President Iliana Yotova 57.6% and Andrey Gyurov 39.5%, AP reported.
The CEC's Monday data showed the Yotova-Valchev ticket with 1,093,852 votes, a margin of 343,601 over the Gyurov-Kandev ticket, which had 750,251, Novinite reported.
Gyurov conceded defeat on Sunday, as initial counts had already shown. If confirmed, Yotova, 62, is Bulgaria's first elected female head of state.
Overseas voters favored Gyurov. The CEC's overseas tally gave his ticket 56.4%, while in Russia Yotova's ticket won 84%, Novinite reported.
body:
Acting President Iliana Yotova has won Bulgaria's presidential runoff, with all votes counted on Monday, the Central Election Commission said, according to the Associated Press. Yotova secured 57.6% of the vote, while Andrey Gyurov, the candidate of the liberal, pro-Western opposition, received 39.5%. Gyurov had conceded defeat on Sunday, when initial counts first showed her ahead.

## Official count

CEC data published Monday morning showed the Yotova-Valchev ticket with 1,093,852 votes, or 57.566%. The Gyurov-Kandev ticket received 750,251 votes, or 39.483%, and 56,080 voters, or 2.951%, selected "I do not support anyone," according to Novinite, which cited the CEC. The margin was 343,601 votes.

The CEC's last reported turnout figure was 19.33% as of 4 p.m. on Nov. 1, when 1,282,848 of 6,637,274 eligible voters had cast ballots, Novinite reported.

## Overseas and the Russia question

Voters abroad leaned the other way. With all overseas protocols processed, the Gyurov-Kandev ticket received 60,413 votes, or 56.363%, against 44,413 votes, or 41.435%, for Yotova and Valchev, Novinite reported. In the United States, Gyurov and Kandev took 67.5%. In Russia, Yotova and Valchev won 84%, against 13.7% for their opponents.

Yotova favors dialogue with Moscow and opposes military aid to Ukraine, according to Le Monde and Deutsche Welle coverage of the race. Her backers included Radev's Progressive Bulgaria party, which holds 131 of 240 seats in parliament, an outright majority, AP and Euronews reported.

## What comes next

The presidency is largely ceremonial. Yotova took over in January when Rumen Radev stepped down to run for parliament. In her victory remarks she said she would work for national consensus by bridging political divisions, NBC News reported.

## The campaign

The runoff was held after a first round on Oct. 25, which Yotova won by a narrow margin, Deutsche Welle reported. The race was framed by Bulgaria's stance on the war in Ukraine. Gyurov, a former interim prime minister, ran as the candidate of the reformist, pro-Western opposition. Yotova, who had succeeded Radev as acting president, ran with the backing of his Progressive Bulgaria party, which controls a majority in parliament.

Monday's count also drew attention to the vote abroad. Gyurov's ticket carried most overseas ballots, but not enough to change the national outcome, according to the CEC tallies reported by Novinite.

## Context

Bulgaria's presidency is largely ceremonial, with the government and parliament holding most executive power. The official results confirm the initial counts reported on Sunday, which had already shown Yotova ahead by a wide margin.
